name: issue_1209_transient_blip_warm_day_self_resolves
description: Issue #1209: warm day (classifier derives hvac_mode=off, comfort band armed, CA commanding cool at the 74F ceiling). The thermostat glitches to heat and returns to cool within the 10-minute confirm window; it must self-resolve with no override. Currently FAILS on production: at 10:10 the blip is confirmed as an override (override_confirmed), so the automation stands down for a transient glitch the occupant never made.
notes: Reproduces Issue #1209 (bug-reproducing scenario, expected to FAIL at 10:10 until production is fixed; verdict.type=negative so simulate.py reports EXPECTED FAIL).
Occupant outcome: a momentary thermostat glitch is mistaken for the occupant's own change; the system then treats it as a manual override and stops managing comfort for the grace period.

Derived from override_self_resolve_transient (golden), which covers the same blip on a HOT day (hvac_mode=cool), where it passes; on a warm day the classifier label is off and production confirms the override instead of self-resolving.
Promote to golden/ once Issue #1209 is fixed and this scenario passes.

events.note: Warm-day classification (hvac_mode left to classifier.py, off): comfort band armed, active ceiling comfort_cool=74F.
Transient: thermostat briefly reports heat mode. Override detection fires; 10-min confirm window starts.
Thermostat returns to cool mode before 10:05 (transient glitch resolved)
Thermostat returns to cool mode at 10:05 — only 5 minutes elapsed, before confirm window expires. Override self-resolves.
30-min classification cycle. Override should NOT be active — classification should apply normally.

assertions.reason: Initial cool-day classification applied: hvac_mode=cool, target=comfort_cool=74F.
Thermostat changed to heat while classification says cool — pending override detection.
assertions.note: Override detection fires in coordinator _async_thermostat_changed listener.

assertions.reason: Confirm timer (override_confirm_seconds=600) fires at 10:10 — 10 minutes after detection at 10:00. Reads current thermostat state (still 'cool', set at 10:04:59) which matches classification.hvac_mode ('cool') — self-resolve path (PATH B in _confirm_override_expired), no override accepted. Corrected from 10:05 — see notes.
assertions.note: Self-resolve genuinely happens at real timer expiry, not proactively on return-to-expected.

assertions.reason: Override was not confirmed (self-resolved), so classification cycle at 10:30 applies normally — not suppressed.

verdict.summary: Issue #1209: a transient thermostat blip on a warm day is confirmed as an override instead of self-resolving
verdict.expected_behavior: override_self_resolved at 10:10: CA distinguishes transient thermostat glitches from real user overrides using the 10-min confirmation window
